claude.sample_unit: simulated clinical vignettes (each in Portuguese and English)

links.outcome: Standalone LLM agreement with reference versus individual clinicians without AI on ESC risk category
links.effect: Pooled clinician benchmark κw 0.52 (95% CI 0.28-0.67); five of eleven LLMs equalled or exceeded it; best GPT-4o κw 0.69. Human-AI team not tested.
links.quote: Notably, five of eleven LLMs equalled or exceeded this pooled clinician benchmark, suggesting that top-performing models reach the performance level of the average individual physician on this task.

links.outcome: LLM performance compared with clinicians on the same vignettes for ESC risk classification
links.effect: Eight clinicians pooled κw 0.52 (0.28-0.67); best LLM GPT-4o κw 0.69 (0.44-0.84); clinicians made no major two-class errors whereas several LLMs did.
links.quote: Notably, five of eleven LLMs equalled or exceeded this pooled clinician benchmark, suggesting that top-performing models reach the performance level of the average individual physician on this task.

links.outcome: Numeric SCORE2 estimation accuracy and internal consistency of LLM calculations
links.effect: MAE 1.22 to 3.16 percentage points across models; bias toward underestimation; numeric-category agreement ranged from 37.5% to 85.0%; deterministic recalculation raised κw to 0.85-0.90.
links.quote: Mean absolute error (MAE) ranged from 1.22 percentage points for Claude Sonnet 4.5 (95% CI, 0.53–2.29; n = 18) to 3.16 for Gemini 2.0 Flash (95% CI, 2.44–3.87; n = 38), with all models exceeding one percentage point on average.

links.outcome: Agreement with gold standard after deterministic external SCORE2 recalculation versus native model output
links.effect: Deterministic κw 0.85-0.90 versus original 0.15-0.61 in eligible vignettes; all eleven models improved, Δκw +0.29 to +0.72.
links.quote: Deterministic risk recalculation yielded substantially and consistently higher agreement with the Gold Standard across all models ( Table 5 ).

links.outcome: Accuracy of guideline-based risk classification and direction of errors
links.effect: κw 0.40-0.69; accuracy 42%-67%; ten of eleven models systematically underestimated risk; major errors in six models (GPT-5 Nano 13%).
links.quote: Ten of eleven models systematically underestimated risk, with the sole exception being Claude Sonnet 4.5, which overestimated more frequently.

links.outcome: Performance consistency across Portuguese and English versions of same vignettes
links.effect: Risk factor Micro-F1 >0.95 in both languages; largest κw difference 0.22 (Llama 3.3); no significant language effects after FDR correction. Repeated-run reproducibility untested.
links.quote: No statistically significant language effects were identified after FDR correction.

links.outcome: Suitability of LLM final risk categorization as stand-alone tool
links.effect: Only moderate final classification agreement and major errors in six models; authors conclude LLMs suit supervised augmentation, not autonomous end-to-end risk stratification.
links.quote: LLMs may therefore already have practical value as supervised tools for information structuring and eligibility assessment, but not as autonomous end-to-end risk stratification systems.

links.outcome: Model handling of uncertain or missing inputs, including withholding classification
links.effect: GPT-5 withheld classification in four vignettes lacking smoking status; Llama 3.3 and GPT-5 Nano omitted classifications for one and five vignettes without explanation.
links.quote: GPT-5 withheld classification in four vignettes where smoking status was absent; Llama 3.3 70B Instruct and GPT-5 Nano omitted classifications for one and five vignettes, respectively, without explanation.

links.quote: Overall classification accuracy ranged from 67% (GPT-4o) to 42% (GPT-5 Nano).

links.effect: Deterministic κw 0.85–0.90; Δκw positive in all models, with CIs excluding zero in 9/11.
links.quote: Deterministic κw clustered narrowly between 0.85 and 0.90, and all eleven models showed a positive Δκw—with confidence intervals excluding zero in nine of eleven models.

links.effect: Five of eleven LLMs equalled or exceeded the pooled clinician benchmark.
links.quote: Notably, five of eleven LLMs equalled or exceeded this pooled clinician benchmark, suggesting that top-performing models reach the performance level of the average individual physician on this task.

links.effect: Risk-classification Δκw ranged −0.16 to +0.22; no statistically significant effects after FDR.
links.quote: No statistically significant language effects were identified after FDR correction.

links.outcome: Missed guideline-specified contraindications and exceptions to risk score calculation
links.effect: Missed exceptions were uncommon across 10 of 11 models, but reached 15.0% (95% CI 0.0-38.5%) in Gemini 2.0 Flash.
links.quote: Missed exceptions were uncommon for all models except with Gemini 2.0 Flash (15.0%, 95% CI: 0.0–38.5%).

screen.practice: deterministic recalculation of risk score outside the LLM
screen.reason: Evaluates LLMs on cardiovascular risk stratification vignettes compared to clinicians and tests post-hoc deterministic recalculation of risk scores using extracted variables as a safeguard against calculation errors.
